fixture.event_delivery: owned Nextcloud container ran repository deliver-events command in a manually launched loop with 5-second sleep
fixture.measurement_pattern: sequential; previous event applied before each next PUT

method.start: host monotonic timestamp just before WebDAV PUT
method.durable_job: first observed dispatched watermark covering the latest file outbox hint, plus linked source sync_logs row
method.publication: first observed published source candidate with current ETag, completed parse, ready chunk, enabled embedding; PDF ready chunk also contained protected synthetic marker
method.applied: first observed WeKnora applied watermark covering the latest file outbox hint
method.timing_interpretation: all observed durations are upper bounds including WebDAV, event-ID lookup, HTTP/SQL query time and polling
method.sync_log_duration_interpretation: successful source scan duration; parsing and publication continue asynchronously

limits: Only three sequential tiny files were measured; no sustained P95, 10,000-file/100-GB capacity or upload-latency comparison follows.
The synthetic LDAP and mock embedding exclude real enterprise AD and model throughput.
The manually launched delivery loop used the production worker command and five-second sleep, but the fixture did not include the dedicated Compose event-worker service.
The existing WeKnora image carries a different patch SHA-256 from the current worktree and cannot certify the current RAG patch.
The PDF was born-digital; scanned-PDF OCR, Office formats, large files, concurrent writes and failure recovery were not measured.
The observation gap between publication and applied watermark is 6.25–8.73 seconds across these samples; its internal cause was not isolated.
